title: Can you prove AI ROI in Software Eng? (Stanford 120k Devs Study) – Yegor Denisov-Blanch, Stanford
talk_summary: A Stanford study of 120k devs measures AI productivity via an ML model replicating expert panels, finding median ~10% gains but wide variance driven by codebase hygiene and usage quality, not token spend. A case study shows PR counts rose 14% after AI adoption while code quality fell 9% and rework rose 2.5x, with effective output flat — meaning naive metrics hide negative ROI.

takeaways.technique: Measure effective output, not PR/commit counts
takeaways.what_they_do: They score engineering output with a model replicating expert panels across implementation time, maintainability, and complexity, and decompose monthly output into added/removed/rework/refactoring buckets instead of counting PRs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: PRs went up by 14%. But this is inconclusive because more PRs doesn't mean better.
takeaways.numbers: PRs +14%, code quality -9%, rework 2.5x, effective output flat

takeaways.technique: Guardrail metrics alongside a primary metric
takeaways.what_they_do: They pair a primary output metric with guardrail metrics (rework/refactoring, quality/tech risk, people/devops) that should be kept healthy but not maximized, to avoid Goodharting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the goal here might be to keep your guardrail metrics healthy while increasing the primary metric

takeaways.technique: Codebase hygiene index as an AI-leverage multiplier
takeaways.what_they_do: They compute an environment cleanliness index (tests, types, docs, modularity, code quality) and find it correlates ~0.40 R² with AI productivity lift; clean code amplifies AI gains and unchecked AI accelerates entropy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: invest in codebase hygiene to unlock these AI productivity gains

takeaways.technique: Usage quality over token volume; watch the 'death valley'
takeaways.what_they_do: Token spend per engineer correlates only ~0.20 with productivity, with a dip around 10M tokens/month, suggesting more spend isn't better and misallocated usage hurts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI usage quality matters more than AI usage value

takeaways.what_they_do: They scan git history for AI fingerprints and grade teams on levels 0-4: no AI, personal unshared prompts, team-shared prompts/rules, autonomous task AI, full agentic orchestration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Level two is team use whereby teams are are sharing these kind of prompts and rules.

takeaways.what_they_do: They note ROI assumes the product function can channel extra engineering capacity into value; otherwise it's a product problem, not an engineering one.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this is assuming that our product function can properly direct that increased capacity into something that generates value
